_comment: What starts what. Reference material for your IaC — no code reads this file.
There is no EventBridge here: the Step Functions state machine drives the whole
chain, including the producer Lambda. That leaves exactly one thing to schedule
from outside — the state machine itself — instead of three rules to keep in step.
The trade is latency on the file drops. A partner file is no longer picked up
seconds after it lands; it waits for the next run of the chain. If that matters,
the answer is an S3 notification to a small Lambda that calls StartExecution.
The only thing that needs an external trigger. Start it however your account
already schedules work — a cron on a build server, an operator clicking Start
Execution, or the scheduler your platform team provides.
`process_date` is the partition every job downstream restricts itself to.
state_machine.name: ecommerce-medallion-pipeline
state_machine.cadence: once a day, after the day is closed in UTC

_comment: Source 1 — the streaming path, and the one trigger that is *not* the state
machine's: SQS pushes to the Lambda as messages arrive, which is the point of
ReportBatchItemFailures is what makes a partial batch failure retry only the
affected messages instead of all ten.
Catalog the lake so Athena can query it without a schema per query. Crawl
silver and gold only — bronze is raw by definition and its schema is allowed
glue_crawlers.name: ecommerce-lake-crawler
